title: Such a grand household, such stinginess
literal_meaning: Pumpkin vine! A son of a grand household, so miserly!
explanation: The rhyme of ଡ଼ଙ୍କ and ରଙ୍କ gives the complaint a teasing snap. A grand household suggests resources, yet its son behaves as though even a small contribution is too much. The joke exposes that mismatch between the family’s impressive image and the person’s stinginess. Here the dictionary places ରଙ୍କ under “miserly”, not “poor”; lack of generosity and lack of money must not be confused.
meaning_odia: କଖାରୁଡ଼ଙ୍କ ସହ ରଙ୍କର ମିଳ ଅଭିଯୋଗଟିକୁ ଟାହିର ସ୍ୱର ଦିଏ। ବଡ଼ଘରର ପୁଅ ବୋଲି ନାମ ଅଛି, ଅଥଚ ସାମାନ୍ୟ କିଛି ଦେବାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ହାତ ଖୋଲୁନାହିଁ—ହସଟି ଏହି ଅମେଳରେ। ଘରର ବଡ଼ ନାମ ଓ ମଣିଷର ଛୋଟ ବ୍ୟବହାରକୁ ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖି କଥାଟି କହାଯାଇପାରେ। ଏଠି ରଙ୍କର ଅଭିଧାନ ଅର୍ଥ କୃପଣ; ଟଙ୍କାର ଅଭାବକୁ କୃପଣତା ସହ ମିଶାଇବା ଠିକ୍ ହେବ ନାହିଁ।
english_summary: A grand family name makes a small act of stinginess look all the more ridiculous.
odia_summary: ବଡ଼ଘରର ନାମ ଓ ସାମାନ୍ୟ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚରେ କୃପଣତା—ଏହି ଅମେଳକୁ କଥାଟି ଟାହି କରେ।
usage_example: At a shared picnic, someone boasts about the size of his family home but refuses to contribute even a few cups. A friend says, “କଖାରୁଡ଼ଙ୍କ ! ବଡ଼ଘରପୁଅ ଏଡ଼ିକି ରଙ୍କ !” The teasing targets his conduct, not someone unable to afford a contribution. (Original imagined example.)
cultural_context: Source sense1 supports stinginess. The household label is the speaker’s taunt, not a rule about class.
